_comment: Short 5 in docs/CONTENT.md: balance billing, and the sentence to read down the phone. The payload is the sentence, not the explanation.
_injury: Fell off a ladder, arm in a sling: already treated, now arguing about the bill.
_stakes: The highest-stakes Short in the set: it tells someone not to pay a bill. Two consequences. (1) The limit is said in the second line, not buried: this is about a provider IN your network. (2) The disclaimer is DRAWN, in words on the board, not left to a description nobody opens.
_numbers: Three, all round: charged $1,000, allowed $400, and the $600 between them. The sentence deliberately says 'what I owe' instead of a fourth figure.
_accuracy: In-network providers accept the allowed amount by contract, so the difference is written off, not billed. Out of network the rules differ, which k8 says rather than implies; emergencies and out-of-network care at in-network facilities have their own protections and are left to another Short.

variants.sling: You fell off a ladder and broke your arm. Insurance paid its share. Then the clinic billed you for the rest.

body.text: That has a name. It is balance billing, and if the clinic is in your network, it is not allowed.
Here is what happened. The clinic charged a thousand dollars.
Your insurance letter says the allowed amount is four hundred.
That six hundred dollar difference is the discount the clinic agreed to when it joined the network.
So it comes off the bill. It does not come to you.
Call the number on the bill, and read this out.
You are in my network. My EOB says what I owe. Please correct the balance. Out of network, the rules are different.
Check yours before you dispute. Or upload them free at UseClaimRight.com.

_pronunciation: 'EOB' is written as one word: Studio-Q reads it as letters, verified by synthesising it and running Whisper back over it. Spelling it 'E O B' made the caption break the letters across lines.
